scope_limits: The primary comparison uses the earlier accepted r98 baseline and a fresh r103 run of the same three-proof workload. Inputs, geometry, proof count, CPU preparation, cache behavior and memory limits match. This is a before/after comparison across revisions, not a simultaneous randomized comparison or confidence interval.
The three independent recursive proofs cover the same twelve native graph leaves. Native proofs are revalidated archives; transaction generation and a complete fresh N3/N4 workflow are excluded.

The primary completion timing starts with CPU preparation after GPU context initialization. The r103 process guard took 90.23 seconds, including first compilation of the changed OpenCL kernel source, versus 57.40 seconds for the earlier warmed r98 process. The 51.26-second pipeline result does not establish a cold-start improvement.

The compiled-source identity changes with the backend implementation. AIR constraints, recursion layout, security profile and transcript protocol source hashes are unchanged by this pass; this does not close the earlier complete-tree soundness and zero-knowledge review gaps.

Coefficient storage is attempt-local, private GPU storage and is dropped when the quotient operation ends. Opening groups combine adjacent compatible single-point matrices using their original alpha exponents. Multi-point and incompatible openings retain sequential reduction. No private values or randomness are shared across proofs.

Reuse is selected automatically when its full live memory plan fits. The original bounded schedule handles tighter memory budgets and single-coset cases. Device-only arithmetic and independent CPU verification remain mandatory.
The checks qualify this Linux OpenCL path. They do not qualify macOS or CUDA, every heterogeneous sixteen-leaf group, or a complete aggregate.

The first final SHAKE check hit the 37-second runtime cap imposed by the remaining ledger and its 30-second cleanup reserve. The user authorized a further two minutes; only that check was retried with a 90-second cap. Both receipts are preserved.
